neet_phy_u16_t13_1.working: Brewster's law: tan i = n = √3, so i = 60°.

neet_phy_u16_t13_2.working: The first polaroid passes I0/2. Malus's law at the second gives (I0/2)cos²30° = (I0/2)(3/4) = 3I0/8.

neet_phy_u16_t13_3.working: At the Brewster angle i + r = 90°, so i = 90° − 37° = 53°. Then n = tan 53° = 4/3.

neet_phy_u16_t13_4.working: A: one polaroid gives I0/2 (III). B: crossed polaroids give 0 (II). C: (I0/2)cos²45° = I0/4 (IV). D: (I0/2)(1/2)(1/2) = I0/8 (I).

neet_phy_u16_t13_5.working: A is true (sound is longitudinal). B is true (vibrations are perpendicular to the plane of incidence). C is false: tan⁻¹1.5 ≈ 56.3°. D is true. E is false: the transmitted intensity stays I0/2 at all orientations. So A, B and D only.
